When dredging in reaches or conditions determined to be non-
standard by the Contracting Officer and the minimum production

without adjustment for performance, provided that the Contractor

and the Contracting Officer concurs that the Contractor has in
fact made such satisfactory effort.

rows.verbatim: Submerged pumps shall meet the following conditions in order for the dredge to be classified as utilizing a submerged pump:

rows.normalized: The cutterhead ladder must be long enough to provide a uniform channel depth of 67 feet.

rows.normalized: Spuds must be long enough to dredge in water depths from 11 to 70 feet.

rows.verbatim: The dredge shall be capable, from each setting of the spud, of dredging a channel at least 300 foot wide, while swinging through an arc of 35 degrees to either side of the centerline of the cut (total arc 70 degrees or less) while at a depth of 67 feet, measured from the water surface.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be capable of dredging a channel at least 300 feet wide within a 70-degree total swing arc at 67-foot depth from each spud setting.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall fulfill the requirements of this subparagraph and subparagraph (a) while achieving or exceeding the minimum production rate requirements listed in the tables at the end of the applicable Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must fulfill dredge capability requirements while achieving or exceeding minimum production rates in the Dredging Region Section tables.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall have available for use at all times a variety of interchangeable pump impellers to permit the dredge to operate under the varying conditions described in the applicable Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must always have available a variety of interchangeable pump impellers.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor at all times shall have available

rows.normalized: Contractor must have available replacement blades, knives, and wipers for the dredge pump/cutter.

rows.verbatim: The dredge shall be equipped with recording vacuum and pressure gauges and a print out of the electronic data recording of engine and pump functions and a pump engine recording tachometer.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be equipped with recording vacuum/pressure gauges, an electronic data printout, and a recording tachometer.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall deliver completed recordings to the Inspector on watch at the time of removal from the recording devices, each day of operation.

rows.verbatim: The dredge shall be equipped with a gyro compass.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be equipped with a gyro compass.

rows.verbatim: All gauges, meters, and other dredging sensory equipment, shall have a valid and current calibration certificate sticker.
rows.normalized: All dredging sensory equipment must have a valid, current calibration certificate sticker.

rows.verbatim: Re-calibration where applicable and as necessary shall be performed whenever dredging conditions change in a manner affecting equipment calibration.
rows.normalized: Contractor must re-calibrate equipment whenever dredging conditions change in a way affecting calibration.

rows.verbatim: Dredging sensory equipment shall be in good operating condition during dredging, and shall be mounted in plain sight of the dredge leverman.
rows.normalized: Dredging sensory equipment must be in good operating condition and mounted in plain sight of the leverman.

rows.verbatim: The dredge leverman shall use the aforementioned required gauges, meters, and all other available sensory equipment, to maximize dredge production during dredging operations.
rows.normalized: The dredge leverman must use required gauges/meters and available sensory equipment to maximize production.

rows.verbatim: The dredge shall be equipped with a degasser.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be equipped with a degasser.

rows.verbatim: Attendant plant shall be composed of such fuel barges, derrick barges, water barges, and other attendant or auxiliary plant as may be required for operations under these specifications, whether or not items are specifically mentioned.
rows.normalized: Contractor's attendant plant must include fuel barges, derrick barges, water barges, and other equipment as required for operations.

rows.verbatim: The attendant plant shall be in good condition and of sufficient size and capacity to efficiently serve the dredge.
rows.normalized: Attendant plant must be in good condition and sufficiently sized/capacitated to serve the dredge.

rows.verbatim: Fuel barges and water barges shall comply with applicable US Coast Guard and US Public Health Service Regulations.
rows.normalized: Fuel and water barges must comply with applicable USCG and US Public Health Service regulations.

rows.verbatim: All skiffs used on this contract shall have a minimum hull length of 22 feet.
rows.normalized: All skiffs used on the contract must have a minimum hull length of 22 feet.

rows.verbatim: The attendant plant shall include a minimum of two tenders per dredge for 24 hours a day operations.
rows.normalized: Attendant plant must include at least two tenders per dredge for 24-hour operations.

rows.verbatim: Each of the tenders shall be a minimum length of 35 feet, have twin screws, inboard, diesel powered engines with a minimum of 140 horsepower on each screw, and shall be capable of working efficiently in the water depths for the particular dredging region where work is assigned.
rows.normalized: Each tender must be at least 35 feet long, twin-screw diesel powered with minimum 140 hp per screw, and capable of working in assigned water depths.

rows.verbatim: They shall be maintained in operating condition at all times regardless of the pay status of the dredge.
rows.normalized: Tenders must be maintained in operating condition at all times regardless of dredge pay status.

rows.verbatim: On dredges equipped with and using a ladder pump, the vacuum gage and vacuum chart will not be required.
rows.normalized: For dredges equipped with and using a ladder pump, the vacuum gauge and vacuum chart are not required.

rows.verbatim: The Government Inspector may require the Contractor to perform a new calibration on this equipment if the Inspector suspects output data from this equipment to be inaccurate.
rows.normalized: If the Inspector suspects the equipment's output data is inaccurate, the Contractor must perform a new calibration when the Government Inspector requires it.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall furnish, throughout the contract period, for the exclusive use of the Government, one diesel or gasoline powered crew boat, with twin propellers, capable of maintaining and traveling no less than the minimum speed of 25 miles per hour / 22 knots, not less than 40 feet in overall length, with enclosed space for at least six passengers after installation of all required equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish a crew boat throughout the contract period meeting specified speed, length, and capacity requirements for exclusive Government use.

rows.verbatim: The crew boat shall meet or exceed all applicable US Coast Guard regulations for vessels 65 feet or less in length, and shall be certified by the US Coast Guard.
rows.normalized: The crew boat must meet or exceed applicable USCG regulations and be USCG certified.

rows.verbatim:
The crew boat shall be equipped with the following:
(1) air conditioning and heating;
(2) VHF FM marine radio transceiver for ship to ship
communications, described in the paragraph entitled
"Communications Equipment";
(3) Navigation radar, as described in the paragraph entitled
"Navigation Radar";
(4) Safety equipment meeting the inspection requirements of the US
Coast Guard Auxiliary and EM 385-1-1.
(5) Global Positioning Equipment (GPS), as described in the
paragraph entitled "Global Positioning System (GPS) Equipment".
rows.normalized: The crew boat must be equipped with AC/heating, VHF radio, navigation radar, USCG-required safety equipment, and GPS.

rows.verbatim: Equipment, which fails to perform because of insufficient power or other mechanical deficiencies, or due to inexperienced operators, shall be replaced, or the operator replaced, as the case may be, within 12 hours after the Contractor is directed to do so by the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must replace failing equipment or operator within 12 hours of COR direction.

rows.verbatim: The crew boat will be used solely for providing the Government Inspectors and Government Agents transportation, and not for conducting surveys, providing transportation for the Contractor's personnel, or transporting the Contractor's supplies.
rows.normalized: Contractor must restrict crew boat use solely to Government Inspector/Agent transportation, not for surveys or Contractor personnel/supplies.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall make provisions to obtain a separate crew boat or vessel for conducting Contractor-related operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain a separate crew boat/vessel for its own operations.

rows.verbatim: The minimum full time crew for the crew boat shall be one operator.
rows.normalized: The crew boat must have at least one full-time operator.

rows.verbatim: The crew boat shall be operated and available 24 hours a day.
rows.normalized: The crew boat must be operated and available 24 hours a day.

rows.verbatim: Smoking shall not be allowed inside the cabin and operator's space while occupied by Government personnel.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not allow smoking inside the cabin/operator space while occupied by Government personnel.

rows.verbatim: NO SMOKING signs shall be posted.
rows.normalized: Contractor must post NO SMOKING signs.

rows.verbatim: The service of one or more towboats, in addition to the regularly assigned plant, shall be required to provide towing service as described in the paragraph entitled "Dredge Towing Service Item".
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide one or more towboats in addition to regularly assigned plant to provide towing service.

rows.verbatim: The towboat(s) shall have horsepower to provide a minimum towing speed of three miles per hour upriver against a current of five miles per hour for moving a single tow consisting of the dredge and necessary attendant plant to commence dredging at a new location.
rows.normalized: Towboats must have horsepower to achieve minimum 3 mph towing speed upriver against a 5 mph current.

rows.verbatim: Further, the towboat(s) utilized shall be capable of safely handling and moving the dredge and attendant plant in currents of up to five miles per hour.
rows.normalized: Towboats must be capable of safely handling/moving the dredge and attendant plant in currents up to 5 mph.

rows.verbatim: The towboat shall have radio equipment to communicate with other vessels in the vicinity of the dredge.
rows.normalized: The towboat must have radio equipment to communicate with nearby vessels.

rows.verbatim: capable of maintaining and traveling no less than the minimum speed of 25 miles per hour / 22 knots
rows.normalized: The Contractor's crew boat must be capable of maintaining and traveling no less than 25 miles per hour / 22 knots.

rows.verbatim: not less than 40 feet in overall length
rows.normalized: The Contractor's crew boat must be not less than 40 feet in overall length.

rows.verbatim: All discharge pipeline shall be maintained in good condition.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain all discharge pipeline in good condition.

rows.verbatim: Leaks occurring in the pipeline shall be promptly stopped.
rows.normalized: Contractor must promptly stop pipeline leaks.

rows.verbatim: For floating pipeline equipment, the Contractor shall provide one 90 degree swivel elbow and one rigid elbow.
rows.normalized: If floating pipeline equipment is used, Contractor must provide one 90-degree swivel elbow and one rigid elbow.

rows.verbatim: While in use, the pipeline shall be secured at intervals not to exceed 400 feet.
rows.normalized: Pipeline in use must be secured at intervals not exceeding 400 feet.

rows.verbatim: The pipeline shall include two elbow pontoons (one each, right and left).
rows.normalized: The pipeline must include two elbow pontoons (one right, one left).

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall furnish a plate style baffle/spreader system that may be installed on the end of any type discharge pipeline to spread dredge slurry during discharge.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish a plate-style baffle/spreader system for discharge pipeline.

rows.verbatim: When directed by the Government, the baffle/spreader shall be installed and employed to reduce scour at the point of discharge and to control the spread of dredged material entering the disposal area.
rows.normalized: When directed by the Government, Contractor must install and employ the baffle/spreader to reduce scour and control material spread.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide adequate numbers of anchors or skidder barges on the floating pipeline to eliminate the possibility of pipeline separation due to river currents.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide adequate anchors/skidder barges on floating pipeline to prevent separation from currents.

rows.verbatim: Floating pipeline shall have navigation lights as specified in Section 01 35 26, paragraph entitled "Signal Lights".
rows.normalized: Floating pipeline must have navigation lights per Section 01 35 26.

rows.verbatim: Floating pipeline shall be placed to provide a minimum hazard to navigation.
rows.normalized: Floating pipeline must be placed to minimize navigation hazard.

rows.verbatim: Furthermore, the Contractor may be required to disconnect all or part of his pipeline to allow the passage of other vessels, if the pipeline would otherwise be a hazard to navigation.
rows.normalized: If the pipeline would be a navigation hazard, Contractor may be required to disconnect all or part of it to allow vessel passage.

rows.verbatim: If submerged pipeline is used, it shall be placed in such a way that it does not create a hazard to navigation.
rows.normalized: If submerged pipeline is used, Contractor must place it so it does not create a navigation hazard.

rows.verbatim: When the submerged pipeline is placed in shallow water, where the possibility exists for small out board skiffs to cross over the pipeline, the pipeline shall be marked every 150 feet throughout the length of the submerged pipeline with U.S. Coast Guard approved fluorescent buoys and signs stating "DANGER SUBMERGED PIPELINE".
rows.normalized: When submerged pipeline is in shallow water with skiff-crossing risk, Contractor must mark it every 150 feet with USCG-approved fluorescent buoys and warning signs.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide the necessary shore pipeline, and all equipment associated with it, to accomplish the said work.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide necessary shore pipeline and associated equipment.

rows.verbatim: The shore pipeline shall be complete with a Y-valve including a spreader at the end of each discharge point.
rows.normalized: Shore pipeline must include a Y-valve with a spreader at each discharge point.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide construction equipment for conducting all shore operations, as deemed appropriate by the Contractor to accomplish the said work.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide construction equipment for shore operations as it deems appropriate.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor's decision for using any such equipment shall be based on his evaluation of the disposal site, for the determination of equipment suitability, prior to mobilization of such equipment and commencement of dredging.
rows.normalized: Contractor's equipment-use decisions must be based on disposal site evaluation prior to mobilization/dredging.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall minimize use of heavy equipment within wetland development sites.
rows.normalized: Contractor must minimize heavy equipment use within wetland development sites.

rows.verbatim: The equipment required to handle and place shore pipeline shall be in good operating condition at all times regardless of the pay status of the dredge.
rows.normalized: Shore pipeline handling equipment must be kept in good operating condition at all times.

rows.verbatim: This shore pipeline and associated equipment shall be considered as part of the dredge attendant plant.
rows.normalized: Shore pipeline and associated equipment shall be considered part of the dredge attendant plant.

rows.verbatim: All radar equipment used under this contract shall be installed so that it will continue functioning on battery power in the event of generator failure.
rows.normalized: All radar equipment must be installed to continue functioning on battery power if the generator fails.

rows.verbatim: Any additional attendant plant to be operated at night must be radar equipped as well.
rows.normalized: Any additional attendant plant operated at night must also be radar equipped.

rows.verbatim: The crew boat shall be equipped with Global Positioning (GPS) equipment capable of using 12 satellites simultaneously.
rows.normalized: The crew boat must be equipped with GPS capable of using 12 satellites simultaneously.

rows.verbatim: The GPS unit shall be fully gasketed for exposure protection and differential ready with a beacon receiver.
rows.normalized: The GPS unit must be fully gasketed and differential-ready with a beacon receiver.

rows.verbatim: The unit shall have a minimum of 250 alphanumeric waypoints and a minimum of 20 reversible routes and waypoints capability.
rows.normalized: The GPS unit must have at least 250 alphanumeric waypoints and at least 20 reversible routes/waypoints capability.

rows.verbatim: In addition, the unit shall have electronic charting with inland and offshore coverage using the most current imagery available.
rows.normalized: The GPS unit must have electronic charting with inland/offshore coverage using the most current imagery.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be required to furnish, on the request of the Contracting Officer or any inspector:
(1) The use of such boats, boatmen, laborers, and material
forming a part of the ordinary and usual equipment and crew of the
floating plant, as may be reasonably necessary in inspecting and
supervising the work;
(2) Suitable transportation between the worksite and all points
on shore designated by the Contracting Officer, to and from the
various pieces of plant, and to and from the floating discharge
pipeline by means of the required tenders or survey boat.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish, on CO/inspector request, boats/boatmen/laborers/material and suitable transportation as described.

rows.verbatim: Furnish, as required by the inspectors, a competent three-man survey crew at all times, including survey boat operator, to work under the Government Inspector's direction.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish a competent three-man survey crew, including survey boat operator, at all times as required by inspectors.

rows.verbatim: Competent crew shall be knowledgeable in conducting electronic positioning surveys using the Contractor-furnished equipment, tying utility crossings to the baseline, offsetting the utility crossings, and setting dredging location buoys if necessary, without immediate supervision of the Government Inspectors.
rows.normalized: The survey crew must be knowledgeable in electronic positioning surveys, utility crossing work, and buoy setting without immediate Government supervision.

rows.verbatim: The survey crew shall be prepared to perform survey work within a one hour notice from Government Inspectors.
rows.normalized: The survey crew must be prepared to perform survey work within one hour of notice from Government Inspectors.

rows.verbatim: Should the Contractor refuse, neglect, or delay compliance with these requirements, the specific facilities may be furnished and maintained by the Contracting Officer, and the cost will be deducted from any amounts due or to become due the Contractor.
rows.normalized: If Contractor refuses, neglects, or delays compliance, the Government may furnish the facilities itself and deduct the cost from amounts due the Contractor.

rows.verbatim: Substitution of the dredge may be allowed provided the Contractor furnishes written justification, the Contracting Officer agrees in writing to the substitution, and the following conditions are met:
rows.normalized: Dredge substitution is allowed only if Contractor furnishes written justification, CO agrees in writing, and other listed conditions are met.

rows.verbatim: The substitute dredge meets all of the requirements of this contract and that the Contractor submits clear evidence that the substitute dredge meets the plant requirements specified in the paragraph entitled "Size and Equipment of Dredge Plant" and that the substitute dredge performs at the rate set forth in the table located in the applicable Dredging Region Section(s), on work similar to that
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit clear evidence that a substitute dredge meets contract requirements, plant size/equipment requirements, and production rate requirements.

rows.verbatim: The substitute dredge will be ready to begin pumping material as soon as the original dredge is removed from service.
rows.normalized: The Contractor's substitute dredge must be ready to begin pumping material as soon as the original dredge is removed from service.

rows.verbatim: The Government is reimbursed all costs in connection with inspection of the substitute dredge, if such is required.
rows.normalized: Contractor must reimburse the Government all costs of inspecting the substitute dredge, if inspection is required.

rows.verbatim: The substitute dredge is delivered to the worksite before the original dredge is shut down and moved off the worksite. This requirement does not apply to substitutions made during release periods.
rows.normalized: Contractor must deliver the substitute dredge to the worksite before the original dredge is shut down and moved off the worksite, except for substitutions made during release periods.

rows.verbatim: Mobilization and demobilization costs for the substitute dredge shall be borne by the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall bear mobilization and demobilization costs for the substitute dredge.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall submit clear evidence that the additional dredge(s) can perform at the rate(s) shown in the chart(s) in the paragraph entitled "Minimum Production Rate Requirements" located in the Dredging Region Section(s) on work similar to that of this contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit clear evidence that additional dredge(s) can perform at the rates shown in the Minimum Production Rate Requirements chart(s), based on similar work.

rows.verbatim: The additional dredge(s) shall provide its own attendant plant as described in the paragraph entitled "Dredge Attendant Plant" at
rows.normalized: Additional dredge(s) shall provide their own attendant plant as described in the 'Dredge Attendant Plant' paragraph, at no additional cost to the Government (sentence continues across page break).

rows.verbatim: The additional dredge(s) shall provide its own survey equipment as described in Section 35 01 50.73, paragraph entitled "Survey Equipment" at no additional cost to the Government.
rows.normalized: Additional dredge(s) shall provide their own survey equipment as described in the Survey Equipment paragraph, at no additional cost to the Government.

rows.verbatim: The additional dredge(s) shall provide its own dredge discharge pipeline as described in the paragraph entitled "Dredge Discharge Pipeline" at no additional cost to the Government.
rows.normalized: Additional dredge(s) shall provide their own dredge discharge pipeline as described in the Dredge Discharge Pipeline paragraph, at no additional cost to the Government.

rows.verbatim: The additional dredge(s) shall conform to the same environmental requirements of the primary dredge.
rows.normalized: Additional dredge(s) shall conform to the same environmental requirements as the primary dredge.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall furnish and maintain the following communications equipment for the dredge, throughout the period of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish and maintain specified communications equipment for the dredge throughout the contract period.

rows.verbatim: Final approval of the plant will not be made until this equipment is installed and in good working order.
rows.normalized: Government will withhold final approval of the plant until the Contractor installs the communications equipment and it is in good working order.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a portable cellular telephone aboard the dredge, with two rechargeable power packs and all necessary recharging equipment and cables.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a portable cellular telephone with two rechargeable power packs and recharging equipment/cables aboard the dredge.

rows.verbatim: The telephone shall be available for official use by the Government Inspectors on a 24 hour a day basis to exclusively conduct Government business and emergency calls.
rows.normalized: Cellular telephone shall be available 24 hours/day for Government Inspectors' official use for Government business and emergency calls.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide functioning 24-hour satellite telephone service with voice and facsimile capability aboard the dredge located in the Corps of Engineers office.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide functioning 24-hour satellite telephone service with voice/fax capability aboard the dredge.

rows.verbatim: The satellite telephone service shall have, as a minimum, voice capability of 4.8 kb/s (kilobytes per second) voice coding and fax speed of 2.4 kb/s.
rows.normalized: Satellite telephone service shall have, at a minimum, 4.8 kb/s voice coding and 2.4 kb/s fax speed.

rows.verbatim: The satellite telephone shall be made available for official use by the Government Inspectors on a 24-hour per day basis to exclusively conduct Government business and emergency
rows.normalized: Satellite telephone shall be made available 24 hours/day for Government Inspectors' official use for Government business and emergency calls (sentence continues across page break).

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall furnish and maintain one VHF-FM ship's radio transceiver for the dredge, with power not in excess of 25 watts, and output of at least 15 watts on the maritime frequencies of 156.800 (Channel 16) and 156.375 (Channel 67) MHz 16F3 emission, with plus or minus 5 KHz at 100% modulation.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish and maintain a VHF-FM ship's radio transceiver meeting specified power, frequency, and modulation parameters.

rows.verbatim: Marine radio equipment shall be operated in accordance with applicable FCC regulations.
rows.normalized: Marine radio equipment shall be operated in accordance with applicable FCC regulations.

rows.verbatim: The dredge shall be equipped with an Automatic Identification System (AIS) in accordance with the Code of Federal Regulations, 33 CFR 164, reference the note to 164.46(a).
rows.normalized: The dredge shall be equipped with an AIS in accordance with 33 CFR 164.46(a).

rows.verbatim: The system shall be operable at all times throughout the contract period.
rows.normalized: The AIS system shall be operable at all times throughout the contract period.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor's plant shall be used in connection with maintenance dredging operations in the navigable channels of the US Army Engineer District, New Orleans.
rows.normalized: Contractor's plant shall be used for maintenance dredging operations in the navigable channels of the New Orleans District.

rows.verbatim: The work shall consist of removing and satisfactorily disposing of material from the dredging regions described herein or from secondary dredging regions as directed by the Contracting Officer or his/her authorized representative.
rows.normalized: The work shall consist of removing and satisfactorily disposing of material from designated dredging regions as directed.

rows.verbatim: Areas that are affected by any of the Contractor's dredging or disposal practices not performed in accordance with these specifications shall be promptly restored by the Contractor to the original conditions at his own expense.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall promptly restore, at its own expense, areas affected by dredging/disposal practices not performed in accordance with specifications.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall be responsible for detecting and reporting to the Government Inspector, materials or obstructions, located within the assigned dredging areas ahead of dredging operations, which will cause damage, or has the potential to cause damage to the dredge and/or attendant plant and equipment.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor may be required to stop work at any time without completing an assignment.
rows.normalized: The Contractor may be required to stop work at any time without completing an assignment.

rows.normalized: Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer of estimated completion time no less than 24 hours prior to completion of dredging operations, during business hours and not later than noon on Friday.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall endeavor to meet the schedule of dredging operations as determined by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall endeavor to meet the dredging schedule determined by the Contracting Officer.

rows.verbatim: Operations shall be performed 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including those days, which have been declared by Congress to be legal holidays for per diem employees of the Federal Government.
rows.normalized: Operations shall be performed 24/7 including federal holidays.

rows.verbatim: Repetitive assignments may be required at the same locations.
rows.normalized: The Contractor may be required to perform repetitive dredging assignments at the same locations.

For a dredge with an inoperable submerged pump,
the new unit price per hour for "Barataria Bar Dredging" and "Barataria
Bar Option Dredging" shall be computed as follows:
rows.normalized: If a dredge has an inoperable submerged pump, the new unit price per hour shall be computed per the specified formula.

rows.verbatim:
The work under this contract requires use of the US Army Corps of
Engineers (USACE) National Dredging Quality Management Program (DQM) to
monitor the dredge's status at all times during the contract duration and
manage data history.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use the USACE DQM Program to monitor dredge status and manage data history for the contract duration.

rows.verbatim:
All costs in connection therewith shall be considered a subsidiary obligation of the Contractor and
shall be included in the contract unit price per hour for the applicable
"Dredging" and "Option Dredging" items on the bidding schedule.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall include all DQM-related costs as a subsidiary obligation within the unit price per hour for Dredging/Option Dredging items.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall have a current certification from the DQM Program for
the cutter/suction head hydraulic dredge instrumentation system to be used
under this contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain current DQM Program certification for the dredge instrumentation system used under the contract.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall have a digital copy of the Dredge Plant
Instrumentation Plan (DPIP) on file with the DQM Support Center.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall keep a digital copy of the DPIP on file with the DQM Support Center.

rows.verbatim:
While working on site, the Contractor
shall also maintain on the dredge a copy of the DPIP, which is easily
accessible to Government personnel at all times.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain an accessible copy of the DPIP on the dredge while working on site.

rows.verbatim:
This document
shall accurately describe the sensors used, the configuration of the
system, how sensor data will be collected, how quality control on the
data will be performed, and how the sensors/data-reporting equipment will
be calibrated and repaired if it fails.
rows.normalized: The DPIP shall accurately describe sensors, system configuration, data collection, QC, and calibration/repair processes.

rows.verbatim:
A description of the computed dredge-specific data and how the
sensor data will be transmitted to the DQM database shall also be
included.
rows.normalized: The DPIP shall include a description of computed dredge-specific data and transmission methods to the DQM database.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to the start of work, the Contractor shall submit to the
DQM Support Center any addendum or modifications made to the plan
subsequent to its original submission.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit any DPIP addenda/modifications to the DQM Support Center prior to the start of work.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide, operate, and maintain all hardware and
software to meet these specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, operate, and maintain all hardware and software to meet the specifications.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall also be
responsible for the replacement, repair, and calibration of the sensors
and other necessary data acquisition equipment needed to supply the
required data.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for replacement, repair, and calibration of sensors and data acquisition equipment.

rows.verbatim:
The procedure to complete a repair shall be documented and completed as
soon as practical.
rows.normalized: The repair procedure must be documented and completed as soon as practical.

rows.verbatim:
If repair is not possible within two business days of
any sensor failure, a plan and timeline to complete the repair shall be
submitted.
rows.normalized: If repair is not possible within two business days of a sensor failure, contractor must submit a plan and timeline to complete the repair.

rows.verbatim:
Upon completion of a repair, replacement, installation,
modification, or calibration, the Contractor shall notify the Contracting
Officer's Representative (COR).
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify the COR upon completion of a repair, replacement, installation, modification, or calibration.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall keep a log of sensor repair, replacement,
installation, modification, and calibration in the dredge's onboard copy
of the DPIP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep a log of sensor repair, replacement, installation, modification, and calibration in the dredge's onboard DPIP copy.

rows.verbatim:
The log shall contain a three-year history of sensor
maintenance, including the time of the sensor failures (and subsequent
repairs), the time and results of sensor calibrations, the time of sensor
replacements, and the time that backup sensor systems were initiated to
provide the required data.
rows.normalized: The log must contain a three-year history of sensor maintenance including failures, repairs, calibrations, replacements, and backup system activations.

rows.verbatim:
It shall also contain the name of the person
responsible for the sensor work.
rows.normalized: The log must also contain the name of the person responsible for the sensor work.

rows.verbatim:
Sensors installed shall be capable of collecting parameters within the
specified accuracies and resolutions indicated in the following
subparagraphs and transmit these parameters to the DQM database.
rows.normalized: Installed sensors must be capable of collecting parameters within specified accuracies/resolutions and transmitting them to the DQM database.

rows.verbatim:
All data
shall be transmitted in JSON message bundles.
rows.normalized: All data must be transmitted in JSON message bundles.

rows.verbatim:
Sensor data
shall be transmitted as work event messages, and data which relates to
the operational state of the dredge or its sensors shall be transmitted
as state event messages.
rows.normalized: Sensor data shall be transmitted as work event messages; operational state data shall be transmitted as state event messages.

rows.verbatim:
Every message bundle shall contain descriptive data that relates the
message to a given dredge plant and date/time.
rows.normalized: Every message bundle must contain descriptive data relating the message to a dredge plant and date/time.

rows.verbatim:
The start of a message
bundle shall be identified by the tag "DQM_data".
rows.normalized: The start of a message bundle must be identified by the tag 'DQM_data'.

rows.verbatim:
A message shall consist of an event type and its associated
data (as defined in paragraph entitled "Dredge Events"), a date/time stamp
indicating when the event occurred or started, and a comment providing
clarification or metadata about the situation.
rows.normalized: A message must consist of an event type and associated data, a date/time stamp, and a comment.

rows.verbatim: Sensor data shall be transmitted as work event messages
rows.normalized: Sensor data must be transmitted as work event messages.

rows.verbatim:
data which relates to the operational state of the dredge or
its sensors shall be transmitted as state event messages
rows.normalized: Data relating to the operational state of the dredge or its sensors must be transmitted as state event messages.

rows.verbatim:
The message time shall be reported to the nearest second and referenced
to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time based on a 24-hour format
(YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
rows.normalized: Message time shall be reported to the nearest second in UTC 24-hour format.

rows.verbatim:
In order to ensure accuracy and reliability, the time stamp shall be
synchronized to UTC format from an accurate, unchangeable source (for
example, a GPS National Marine Electronics Association [NMEA]
datastring).
rows.normalized: The time stamp shall be synchronized to UTC from an accurate, unchangeable source.

rows.verbatim:
Message time
shall be identified by the tag "msg_time".
rows.normalized: Message time shall be identified by the tag "msg_time".

rows.verbatim:
A comment shall be identified by the introductory tag
"comment", and the comment shall consist of no more than 250 characters.
rows.normalized: A comment shall be identified by the tag "comment" and shall not exceed 250 characters.

rows.verbatim:
All work event
messages shall be initiated by the header tag "work_event".
rows.normalized: All work event messages shall be initiated by the header tag "work_event".

rows.verbatim:
Sensor values reported in a work event shall represent a weighted average
with the highest and lowest values not included in the calculated average
for the given interval.
rows.normalized: Sensor values reported in a work event shall represent a weighted average excluding the highest and lowest values.

rows.verbatim:
The averaging routine used shall be consistent across all event
triggers.
rows.normalized: The averaging routine used shall be consistent across all event triggers.

rows.verbatim:
This information shall be documented in the DPIP sections that say
"Calculations done external to the instrumentation".
rows.normalized: The averaging routine information shall be documented in the DPIP.

rows.verbatim:
The variation of the water level from the vertical datum for the river
stage or tidal gage described in the state events shall be obtained using
appropriate equipment to give the water level with an accuracy of +/- 0.1
ft.
rows.normalized: Water level variation from vertical datum shall be obtained using equipment accurate to +/- 0.1 ft.

rows.verbatim:
Vertical correction values above project datum described in the dredging
specification shall be entered with a positive sign and those below with
a negative sign.
rows.normalized: Vertical correction values above project datum shall be entered as positive; those below as negative.

rows.verbatim:
The tag for vertical correction shall be
"vert_correction".
rows.normalized: The tag for vertical correction shall be "vert_correction".

rows.verbatim:
The X, Y, and Z components of the cutter/suction head location shall be
monitored.
rows.normalized: The X, Y, and Z components of the cutter/suction head location shall be monitored.

rows.verbatim:
The forwardmost point of the cutter/suction head shall be obtained using a
positioning system operating with a minimum accuracy level of 3-10 feet
horizontal Circular Error Probable (CEP).
rows.normalized: The forwardmost point of the cutter/suction head shall be obtained via a positioning system with a minimum accuracy of 3-10 feet CEP.

rows.verbatim:
It shall be reported as
Latitude/Longitude WGS 84 in decimal degrees with West Longitude and
South Latitude values reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Cutter/suction head position shall be reported as Lat/Long WGS 84 decimal degrees, with West/South as negative.

rows.verbatim:
Position values shall be identified by the tags "ch_latitude" and
"ch_longitude".
rows.normalized: Position values shall be identified by the tags "ch_latitude" and "ch_longitude".

rows.verbatim: Instrumentation shall be capable of reporting to an accuracy of +/- 0.5 foot and a resolution to the nearest 0.1 foot with no tidal adjustments.
rows.normalized: Contractor's instrumentation must report cutter/suction invert depth to +/-0.5 ft accuracy and 0.1 ft resolution.

rows.verbatim: The tag "ch_depth" shall be used to identify the cutter/suction head depth.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use tag "ch_depth" to identify cutter/suction head depth.

rows.verbatim: All headings shall be provided using industry-standard equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide all headings using industry-standard equipment.

rows.verbatim: The heading shall be accurate to within 5 degrees and reported to the nearest whole degree with values from 000 (true north) to 359 degrees referenced to a clockwise positive direction convention.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report heading accurate to 5 degrees, to the nearest whole degree, 000-359 clockwise from true north.

rows.verbatim: The tag "ch_heading" shall be used to identify the cutter/suction head heading.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use tag "ch_heading" for cutter/suction head heading.

rows.verbatim: Dredge activity shall be monitored using a combination of the following parameters.
rows.normalized: Contractor must monitor dredge activity using the listed parameters.

rows.verbatim: A flow-metering device, calibrated according to the manufacturer's specifications, shall be used to record the slurry velocity to the nearest 0.01 fps with an accuracy of +/- 0.1 fps.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use a calibrated flow-metering device to record slurry velocity to 0.01 fps at +/-0.1 fps accuracy.

rows.verbatim: If the manufacturer does not specify a frequency of recalibration, calibration shall be conducted prior to the commencement of work.
rows.normalized: If manufacturer specifies no recalibration frequency for the velocity meter, contractor must calibrate before work begins.

rows.verbatim: The slurry velocity shall be measured for the same pipeline inside diameter as that used for the slurry density measurement.
rows.normalized: Contractor must measure slurry velocity using the same pipeline inside diameter as used for density measurement.

rows.verbatim: The tag "slurry_velocity" shall be associated with this value.
rows.normalized: Contractor must associate tag "slurry_velocity" with the velocity value.

rows.verbatim: A density-metering device, calibrated according to the manufacturer's specifications, shall be used to record the slurry density of material being moved to the nearest 0.01 g/cc.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use a calibrated density-metering device to record slurry density to the nearest 0.01 g/cc.

rows.verbatim: The tag "slurry_density" shall be associated with this value.
rows.normalized: Contractor must associate tag "slurry_density" with the density value.

rows.verbatim: The shaft revolution rate (rev/min) shall be measured with the highest level of accuracy that is standard on the vessel's operational displays either at the bridge or in the engine room.
rows.normalized: Contractor must measure pump shaft rev/min at the highest accuracy standard on vessel displays.

rows.verbatim: This value shall be identified by the tag "rpm".
rows.normalized: Contractor must identify pump RPM value with tag "rpm".

rows.verbatim: The vacuum pressure of the dredge pump(s) (inches of mercury) shall be
rows.normalized: Contractor shall measure/report the vacuum pressure of the dredge pump(s) in inches of mercury (sentence continues on next page).

rows.verbatim: Vacuum pressure shall be identified by the tag "vacuum".
rows.normalized: Contractor must identify vacuum pressure with tag "vacuum".

rows.verbatim: The pump outlet pressure shall be measured in the discharge line on the pump side of the flap valve in terms of pounds per square inch (psi) on a gauge.
rows.normalized: Contractor must measure pump outlet pressure in psi on a gauge on the pump side of the flap valve.

rows.verbatim: Pump outlet pressure shall be identified by the tag "outlet_psi".
rows.normalized: Contractor must identify pump outlet pressure with tag "outlet_psi".

rows.verbatim: The X and Y position of the terminal end of the outfall pipe shall be monitored continuously and the position reported as part of the work event string.
rows.normalized: Contractor must continuously monitor and report outfall pipe end X/Y position in the work event string.

rows.verbatim: The horizontal position of the outfall end of the discharge pipe shall be obtained using a positioning system operating with a minimum accuracy level of 3-10 feet horizontal Circular Error Probable (CEP).
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain discharge pipe outfall horizontal position with a positioning system of at least 3-10 ft CEP accuracy.

rows.verbatim: It shall be reported as Latitude/Longitude WGS 84 in decimal degrees with West Longitude and South Latitude values being reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report outfall position as WGS 84 Lat/Long decimal degrees, with West/South as negative.

rows.verbatim: Position values shall be identified by the tags "outfall_latitude" and "outfall_longitude".
rows.normalized: Contractor must tag position values as "outfall_latitude" and "outfall_longitude".

rows.verbatim: Each type of state event message shall be indicated by a specific header tag as enumerated in the following subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: Contractor must indicate each state event message type with the specific header tag enumerated below.

rows.verbatim: However, they should be sent only if the state value changes.
rows.normalized: Contractor should send state events only when the state value changes.

rows.verbatim: The leverman's time shall be entered to the nearest second as local time and automatically converted to and reported in UTC based on a 24-hour format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter leverman's time to the nearest second local, converted/reported in UTC 24-hour format.

rows.verbatim: Message time shall be identified by the tag "msg_time".
rows.normalized: Contractor must identify message time with tag "msg_time".

rows.verbatim: Information concerning the contract under which dredging is being performed shall be reported at the start and completion of each contract using the header tag "contract_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report contract information at start and completion of each contract using tag "contract_event".

rows.verbatim: The USACE-assigned contract number for the project shall be reported using the tag "contract_number".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report the USACE contract number using tag "contract_number".

rows.verbatim: The start and end of a contract shall be reported using the tag "event_type" with the appropriate value of "start" or "end".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report contract start/end using tag "event_type" with value "start" or "end".

rows.verbatim: Properties associated with the vertical correction (see paragraph entitled "Vertical Correction") for the tide station/river stage gage shall be grouped together under the header tag "station_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor must group tide/river gage vertical correction properties under header tag "station_event".

rows.verbatim: This information shall be sent at the start of the contract and each time the dredge has moved enough to change the station being used.
rows.normalized: Contractor must send station event information at contract start and whenever the station changes.

rows.verbatim: It shall be introduced by the tag "station_name", and it shall consist of a descriptor of no more than 25 characters.
rows.normalized: Contractor must tag station name with "station_name" using a descriptor of no more than 25 characters.

rows.verbatim: The leverman's estimate of the length of pipe downflow from the dredge pump, measured to the nearest whole foot, shall be reported under the header tag "pipe_length_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report leverman's pipe-length estimate to the nearest whole foot under tag "pipe_length_event".

rows.verbatim: This information shall be sent at the start of the contract and at the completion of each 24-hour period ending at midnight local time.
rows.normalized: Contractor must send pipe length event data at contract start and at completion of each 24-hour period ending midnight local.

rows.verbatim: The total length of floating pipe shall be reported with the tag "length_floating".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report total floating pipe length with tag "length_floating".

rows.verbatim: The total length of submerged pipe shall be reported with the tag "length_submerged".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report total submerged pipe length with tag "length_submerged".

rows.verbatim: The total length of shore pipe shall be reported with the tag "length_land".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report total shore pipe length with tag "length_land".

rows.verbatim: Information concerning the booster pumps being used shall be included under the header tag "booster_pump_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor must include booster pump information under header tag "booster_pump_event".

rows.verbatim: A message shall be sent to indicate any change in the status of the booster pumps being used.
rows.normalized: Contractor must send a message whenever booster pump status changes.

rows.verbatim: Upon the addition or removal of a booster pump, the total number of booster pumps being used shall be reported with the tag "booster_total".
rows.normalized: Upon adding/removing a booster pump, contractor must report the total number in use with tag "booster_total".

rows.verbatim: It shall be introduced by the tag "station_name",
rows.normalized: The contractor must label the station name field with the tag "station_name".

rows.verbatim: and it shall consist of a descriptor of no more than 25 characters.
rows.normalized: The contractor must limit the station name descriptor to no more than 25 characters.

rows.verbatim: The dredge advance, the total forward progress of the dredge relative to the centerline of the cut, shall be measured to the nearest whole foot and cumulatively calculated over a 24-hour period from midnight to midnight local time.
rows.normalized: Contractor must measure dredge advance to the nearest whole foot, cumulative over each midnight-to-midnight 24-hour period.

rows.verbatim: It shall be identified by the tag "advance_daily".
rows.normalized: Contractor must identify dredge advance with tag "advance_daily".

rows.verbatim: The msg_time associated with this tag shall be reported as the first timestamp of the following 24-hour period (based on the local time) rather than as midnight of the day for which the value was calculated, and it shall be reported in Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).
rows.normalized: Contractor must report msg_time for dredge advance as the first timestamp of the following period, in GMT.

rows.verbatim: The X and Y position of the terminal end of the outfall pipe shall be monitored and sent at the start of the contract and thereafter according to the following table.
rows.normalized: Contractor must monitor and send outfall pipe end X/Y position at contract start and per the specified table schedule.

rows.verbatim: For beach nourishment, the horizontal X and Y position of the outfall shall be sent at the start of the contract and at the completion of each 24-hour period ending at midnight local time.
rows.normalized: For beach nourishment work, contractor must send outfall X/Y position at contract start and each 24-hour period ending midnight local.

rows.verbatim: Information on where the slurry is being discharged shall be reported with the tag "outfall_location".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report discharge location with tag "outfall_location".

rows.verbatim: The horizontal position of the outfall end of the discharge pipe shall be obtained using a positioning system operating with a minimum accuracy level of 3-10 feet horizontal Circular Error Probable (CEP).
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain discharge outfall horizontal position with a positioning system of at least 3-10 ft CEP accuracy.

rows.verbatim: It shall be reported as Latitude/Longitude WGS 84 in decimal degrees with West Longitude and South Latitude values being reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report discharge horizontal position as WGS 84 Lat/Long decimal degrees, West/South negative.

rows.verbatim: Position values shall be identified by the tags "outfall_latitude" and "outfall_longitude".
rows.normalized: Contractor must tag discharge position values as "outfall_latitude" and "outfall_longitude".

rows.verbatim: All headings shall be provided using industry-standard equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide discharge outfall heading using industry-standard equipment.

rows.verbatim: They shall be accurate to within 5 degrees and reported to the nearest whole degree with values from 000 (true north) to 359 degrees referenced to a clockwise positive direction convention.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report discharge outfall heading accurate to 5 degrees, nearest whole degree, 000-359 clockwise from true north.

rows.verbatim: The discharge heading shall be identified by the tag "outfall_heading".
rows.normalized: Contractor must identify discharge heading with tag "outfall_heading".

rows.verbatim:
The msg_time associated with this tag shall be reported as the first timestamp
of the following 24-hour period (based on the local time) rather than as
midnight of the day for which the value was calculated
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report the msg_time for the advance_daily tag as the first timestamp of the following 24-hour period, not midnight of the calculated day.

rows.verbatim:
and it shall be
reported in Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report the msg_time in Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).

rows.verbatim: The tag "outfall_elevation" shall be used to identify this elevation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use tag "outfall_elevation" to identify discharge pipe elevation.

rows.verbatim: Delays and dredge downtime shall be reported at the conclusion of the event.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report delays and dredge downtime at the conclusion of the event.

rows.verbatim: The reason for the non-effective work time shall be submitted under the header tag "non_eff_event" within 24 hours of the event.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit reason for non-effective work time under tag "non_eff_event" within 24 hours of the event.

rows.verbatim: The start and end times for the non-effective work event shall be reported using the tags "msg_start_time" and "msg_end_time".
rows.normalized: Contractor must report non-effective work event start/end times using tags "msg_start_time" and "msg_end_time".

rows.verbatim: The dredge operator indication of production delays, as listed on Form 4267, shall be transmitted at the end of the non-effective interval.
rows.normalized: Contractor must transmit Form 4267 production delay code at the end of the non-effective interval.

rows.verbatim: Dredge function event messages shall be identified by the tag "function_code" and shall consist of one of the following standardized entries to indicate the operation:
rows.normalized: Contractor must identify dredge function event messages with tag "function_code" using one of the standardized entries listed.

rows.verbatim:
The "comment" tag shall be used to provide additional explanation for the
noted delays or downtimes.
rows.normalized: The Contractor must use the 'comment' tag to provide additional explanation for noted delays or downtimes.

rows.verbatim:
For example, when the code "LDPV" (Loss Due to
Passing Vessel) is indicated, the name of the vessel and the number of
tows shall be listed with the "comment" tag.
rows.normalized: When code LDPV is indicated, the Contractor must list the vessel name and number of tows with the comment tag.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor's DQM system shall be capable of collecting and
transmitting data to the DQM system.
rows.normalized: The Contractor's DQM system must be capable of collecting and transmitting data to the DQM system.

rows.verbatim:
The applicable parameters from paragraph entitled "Requirements for Reported
Data" shall be recorded as events locally and continuously transmitted to
the DQM database anytime an Internet connection is available.
rows.normalized: The Contractor must record applicable parameters as events locally and continuously transmit them to the DQM database whenever an Internet connection is available.

rows.verbatim:
The computer system
shall be a standalone system, exclusive to the DQM monitoring system, and
shall have USACE DQM software installed on it.
rows.normalized: The computer system must be a standalone system exclusive to the DQM monitoring system.

rows.verbatim:
If a hardware
problem occurs, or if a part of the system is physically damaged, then the
Contractor shall be responsible for repairing it within two business days
of the determination of the condition or submitting a plan and timeline
for repair if the repair will take more than two business days.
rows.normalized: If a hardware problem occurs or a part of the system is physically damaged, the Contractor must repair it within two business days of determination, or submit a repair plan/timeline if the repair will take longer than two business days.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide a dedicated onboard computer for use by the
Dredging Quality Management system.
rows.normalized: The Contractor must provide a dedicated onboard computer for the Dredging Quality Management system.

rows.verbatim:
This computer shall run the USACE DQM software and receive data from the
Contractor's data-reporting interface.
rows.normalized: The onboard computer must run the USACE DQM software and receive data from the Contractor's data-reporting interface.

rows.verbatim: This computer must meet or exceed the following performance specifications:
rows.normalized: The onboard computer must meet or exceed the listed performance specifications.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall install a fully licensed copy of Windows 10
Professional Operating System or later on the computer specified above.
rows.normalized: The Contractor must install a fully licensed copy of Windows 10 Professional (or later) on the specified computer.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall also install any necessary manufacturer-provided
drivers for the installed hardware.
rows.normalized: The Contractor must install any necessary manufacturer-provided drivers for the installed hardware.

rows.verbatim: This computer shall be located and oriented to allow data entry and data
rows.normalized: The onboard computer must be located and oriented to allow data entry and data [sentence continues past page break].

rows.verbatim: No other software which conflicts with this function shall be installed on it.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not install conflicting software on the DQM computer.

rows.verbatim: The DQM computer shall also have the USACE-provided Dredging Quality Management Onboard Software (DQMOBS) installed on it by DQM personnel.
rows.normalized: Contractor's DQM computer must have DQMOBS installed by DQM personnel.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall supply an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) for the computer and networking equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must supply a UPS for the computer and networking equipment.

rows.verbatim: It shall interface with the DQM computer to communicate UPS status, and it shall provide backup power at 1 kVA for a minimum of 10 minutes.
rows.normalized: The UPS must interface with the DQM computer for status and provide at least 1 kVA backup power for 10 minutes minimum.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall ensure that sufficient power outlets are available to run all specified equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure sufficient power outlets are available for all specified equipment.

rows.verbatim: A web service shall be used to report sensor data to the DQM database.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use a web service to report sensor data to the DQM database.

rows.verbatim: Data shall be transmitted as it is collected in real time and pushed to the DQM web service.
rows.normalized: Contractor must transmit data in real time as collected to the DQM web service.

rows.normalized: If the web service is unavailable/errors, contractor must queue data and transmit oldest-first upon reconnection until real-time is restored.

rows.normalized: If Option 2 is chosen, contractor must make a display of raw transmitted data easily accessible/visible onboard.

rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain an Internet connection with capacity for real-time transmission plus clearing queued data on reconnection.

rows.verbatim: The telemetry system shall always be available and have connectivity in the contract area.
rows.normalized: Contractor's telemetry system must always be available and connected within the contract area.

rows.verbatim: If connectivity is lost, unsent data shall be queued and transmitted upon restoration of connectivity.
rows.normalized: If connectivity is lost, contractor must queue unsent data and transmit it once connectivity is restored.

rows.verbatim: Delays in pushing real-time data to the DQM database should not exceed four hours.
rows.normalized: Contractor's delays in pushing real-time data to the DQM database should not exceed four hours.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall acquire and install all necessary hardware and software to make the Internet connection available for data transmission to the DQM web service.
rows.normalized: Contractor must acquire and install all hardware/software necessary for Internet connectivity to the DQM web service.

rows.verbatim: The hardware and software shall be configured to allow the DQM Support Center remote access to this computer, and the telemetry system shall be capable of meeting these minimum reporting requirements in all operating conditions.
rows.normalized: Contractor must configure hardware/software for DQM Support Center remote access and ensure telemetry meets minimum reporting requirements in all conditions.

rows.verbatim: In areas with poor cellular service and at the local District's discretion, it may be required to manually download the data on a daily basis using the protocol for retrieving and submitting backup files provided by the DQM Support Center.
rows.normalized: Where cellular service is poor, contractor may be required by the District to manually download data daily per the DQM backup-file protocol.

rows.verbatim: Portions of this Contractor-collected information, as described in this specification, shall be routed to the DQM computer on a real-time basis, utilizing one of the options outlined in paragraphs 3.2.1 "Option 1: Computer Requirements" through 3.2.5 "Internet Access".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall route portions of contractor-collected information to the DQM computer on a real-time basis using one of the options in paragraphs 3.2.1-3.2.5.

rows.verbatim: If the serial transmission option is used, sensor data shall be sent to the DQM computer via an RS-232 serial interface with a baud rate of 9600 or 19200 bps.
rows.normalized: If serial transmission is used, Contractor shall send sensor data to the DQM computer via RS-232 interface at 9600 or 19200 bps.

rows.verbatim: The serial interface shall be configured as 8 bits, no parity, and no flow control.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall configure the serial interface as 8 bits, no parity, no flow control.

rows.verbatim: Information regarding changes in the state of the dredge shall be digitally logged and transmitted as close to the time of the occurrence as possible.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall digitally log and transmit dredge state-change information as close to the time of occurrence as possible.

rows.verbatim: Portions of this Contractor-collected information, as described in this specification, and calculations based on them shall be stored and transmitted to the DQM database on a near real-time basis.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall store and transmit portions of contractor-collected information and related calculations to the DQM database on a near real-time basis.

rows.verbatim: Additionally, information regarding the state of the dredge shall be digitally logged and transmitted.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall digitally log and transmit information regarding the state of the dredge.

rows.verbatim: Data shall be logged as a series of events.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall log data as a series of events.

rows.verbatim: Each event shall consist of a dataset containing dredge information (as defined in paragraph entitled "Requirements for Reported Data").
rows.normalized: Each event shall consist of a dataset containing dredge information as defined in 'Requirements for Reported Data'.

rows.verbatim: Each set of measurements (for example, time and position) shall be considered an event
rows.normalized: Each set of measurements (e.g., time and position) shall be considered a work event.

rows.verbatim: there shall be a 6-12 second interval between work events.
rows.normalized: There shall be a 6-12 second interval between work events.

rows.verbatim: This interval shall remain consistent across event types for the dredge plant.
rows.normalized: The work-event interval shall remain consistent across event types for the dredge plant.

rows.verbatim: A standard data string shall be recorded within one second of an event trigger with the time stamp and all parameters reflecting when the event happened.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall record a standard data string within one second of an event trigger with correct time stamp and parameters.

rows.verbatim: A set of descriptive information (event name, time, description, comment) shall be considered a state event.
rows.normalized: A set of descriptive information (event name, time, description, comment) shall be considered a state event.

rows.verbatim: These events shall be recorded within 24 hours of a change in state with the time stamp reflecting when the event happened.
rows.normalized: State events shall be recorded within 24 hours of a change in state with correct time stamp.

rows.verbatim: The data shall be formatted as JSON (JavaScript Object Notation, as defined at http://www.json.org) strings of arbitrary length.
rows.normalized: Contractor's data shall be formatted as JSON strings of arbitrary length.

rows.verbatim: No "Null" value strings shall be included in a message bundle.
rows.normalized: No 'Null' value strings shall be included in a message bundle.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall maintain an archive of all data sent to the DQM computer during the dredging contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain an archive of all data sent to the DQM computer during the dredging contract.

rows.verbatim: The COR may require, at no increase in the contract price, that the Contractor provide a copy of these data covering specified time periods.
rows.normalized: If the COR requires it, Contractor shall provide a copy of archived data covering specified time periods at no increase in contract price.

rows.verbatim: The data shall be provided in the same JSON format as would have been transmitted to the DQM computer.
rows.normalized: Data provided to the COR shall be in the same JSON format as originally transmitted to the DQM computer.

rows.verbatim: There shall be no line breaks between the parameters
rows.normalized: There shall be no line breaks between the parameters in the data records.

rows.verbatim: each record string shall be on separate line.
rows.normalized: Each record string shall be on a separate line.

rows.verbatim: The naming convention for the files shall be < dredgename>_<StartYYYYMMddhhmmss>_<EndYYYYMMddhhmmss>.txt.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall name backup data files using the convention <dredgename>_<StartYYYYMMddhhmmss>_<EndYYYYMMddhhmmss>.txt.

rows.verbatim: Data submission shall be via a storage medium acceptable to the COR.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit data via a storage medium acceptable to the COR.

rows.verbatim: At the end of the dredging contact, the Contractor shall call the DQM Support Center prior to discarding the data.
rows.normalized: At the end of the dredging contract, Contractor shall call the DQM Support Center before discarding the data.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall record the following information in a separate section at the end of the dredge's onboard copy of the DPIP:
rows.normalized: Contractor shall record specified information in a separate section at the end of the dredge's onboard DPIP copy.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor's National Dredging Quality Management Program's data transmission shall be fully operational at the start of dredging operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor's National Dredging Quality Management Program data transmission shall be fully operational at the start of dredging operations.

rows.verbatim: To meet contract requirements for operability, the Contractor's system shall provide an accurate data string return and be compliant with hardware requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor's system shall provide an accurate data string return and be compliant with hardware requirements to meet operability requirements.

rows.verbatim: Repairs necessary to restore data return compliance shall be made within two business days
rows.normalized: Contractor shall make repairs necessary to restore data return compliance within two business days.

rows.verbatim: a plan and timeline for repair shall be submitted to the DQM Data Acquisition and Analysis Team if the repair will take more than two business days.
rows.normalized: If repair will take more than two business days, Contractor shall submit a plan and timeline for repair to the DQM Data Acquisition and Analysis Team.

rows.verbatim: Failure by the Contractor to report quality data within the specified time window for dredge measurements as stated in the specifications (see paragraphs entitled "Internet Access", "Data Measurement Frequency" and "Parameter Transmission to the Web Service") will result in withholding of up to 10% of the contract progress payment per clause 52.232-5.
rows.normalized: If Contractor fails to report quality data within the specified time window, the Government will withhold up to 10% of the contract progress payment per clause 52.232-5.
